item.title: A User-Item Aware Encoding Framework for Short Video
item.description: arXiv:2611.32187v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Traditional encoding methods from the Professional Generated Content (PGC) era face significant challenges due to two unique characteristics of user-generated short videos: massive daily uploads (reaching hundreds of millions) and heterogeneous content-consumer relationships (varying video quality and diverse consumer contexts). To address these challenges, we propose UIAE (User-Item Aware Encoding), a novel multiple bitrate ladder group encoding method comprising three key components: 1) Establishing user-item relationships via rule-based or DNN-based models; 2) Developing local optimization models maximizing Quality of Experience (QoE) for sub-populations based on contextual consumption patterns; 3) Deriving globally optimal encoding strategies through hierarchical model integration. Experimental results demonstrate that the UIAE framework adaptively adjusts encoding outcomes for distinct user groups with varying context profiles, ensuring optimal QoE for end viewers. We have deployed the UIAE method into the online pipeline, handling tens of millions of video transcoding tasks daily.
item.dc:creator: Weihui Deng, He Liu, Bin Wang, Xiaocheng Li, Deliang Fu, Zhen Wang

item.title: Residual Guidance for Real-Time Interactive Video Generation
item.description: arXiv:2611.32820v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Real-time interactive video generation allows users to change the prompt during generation to steer the evolving video. However, existing streaming models, which generate videos chunk by chunk, often keep following the previous prompt after a switch. We trace this failure to context inertia, where the previous chunk acts as a strong prior that suppresses the new prompt. Furthermore, we find that this inertia persists even when the cache retains only the previous chunk, yet discarding the context breaks visual continuity, which limits approaches that edit the cache. Rather than editing the cache, we propose Residual Guidance (RG), a simple, training-free method that counteracts context inertia with a correction measured outside the cache. Specifically, RG denoises the re-noised previous chunk once under the new prompt without the cache and adds the resulting residual to the early denoising steps of the next chunk, where its content is largely decided and the new prompt is most suppressed. Across settings ranging from a single switch to long multi-switch generation, RG substantially improves prompt switching capability on existing streaming models, including those with dedicated switching mechanisms, while largely retaining visual quality. As it requires no training or per-model tuning and adds only one forward pass per chunk, RG can be easily integrated into existing real-time video generation pipelines.
item.dc:creator: NaHyeon Park, Kyeong-Hwan Moon, Youjin Jeon, Hyunjung Shim

item.title: MSRGF: Multi-Source Reconstruction with Reference-Guided Fusion for Incomplete Multimodal Sentiment Analysis
item.description: arXiv:2611.32860v1 Announce Type: new Abstract: Incomplete multimodal sentiment analysis (MSA) predicts sentiment from textual, acoustic, and visual features when some observations are missing. Existing reconstruction methods estimate missing features from available modalities and combine the resulting information for sentiment prediction. However, different available modalities can produce distinct estimates of the same modality, while direct fusion often leaves the relationships among these estimates underused. We propose MSRGF (Multi-Source Reconstruction with Reference-Guided Fusion), which retains separate estimates and exploits their relationships during fusion. Specifically, MSRGF comprises three components: (1) Source-Wise Reconstruction (SWR), which uses modality-specific queries and a shared generator to produce a separate estimate of each modality from every available modality; (2) Reference-Guided Fusion (RGF), which uses relationships among estimates and available observations to construct a weighted reference, selectively refines it using their differences, and incorporates observed features when available; and (3) Global Context Modulation (GCM), which uses global context to adjust modality summaries for sentiment prediction. Extensive experiments on three datasets show that MSRGF outperforms existing methods, achieving average accuracy improvements of 1.9% on MOSEI under random within-modality missingness, 0.6% under random whole-modality missingness and 1.3% under fixed whole-modality missingness.
item.dc:creator: Yan Zhuang, Minhao Liu, Yanru Zhang, Li Ma, Weilong Chen, Xingyu Wu, Jiawen Deng, Fuji Ren

item.title: Rethinking Video Agents: When and Why Video Harnesses Work
item.description: arXiv:2611.31883v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Video understanding depends not only on how models reason about visual evidence, but also on which evidence they observe. Fixed observation policies determine this evidence in advance; agentic harnesses allow models to seek further observations as their understanding develops. This shift creates an opportunity to realize capabilities that fixed inputs leave untapped, yet the ability to request observations does not ensure their effective use. We investigate when and why video harnesses improve understanding, examining how task demands and models' capacity for interaction jointly shape their benefits. Using Video-Relook as an experimental framework, we let models adapt their temporal and spatial observations from a common default configuration, and analyze performance and interaction trajectories across models and tasks. Adaptive observation yields substantial gains on fine-grained action understanding, with benefits also extending to Video-MME-v2. Even under the same observation interface, gains differ substantially across models; interaction traces reveal corresponding differences in evidence seeking and the reliability of answer revision. The benefits also vary across tasks for the same model, ranging from substantial improvements to limited gains and regressions. Together, these findings support an account in which harness effectiveness depends on the alignment between opportunities for informative observation and the model's ability to turn interaction into reliable revisions. They motivate video harnesses that coordinate perception and reasoning, matching observational autonomy to task demands and model capabilities.
item.dc:creator: Luoyuan Zhang, Xuanyu Zheng, Yancheng Long, Haoyang Xu, Bin Wen, Tingting Gao

item.title: Lossless Re-Encoding of Vorbis and Opus Audio Files
item.description: arXiv:2611.32641v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present Balrogg, a lossless recompressor that replaces the entropy coding of Ogg Vorbis and Ogg Opus files with adaptive context mixing models. For Vorbis, we write each represent each codebook entry as a tuple of small signed integers (digits), binarized in five stages, and mixed with a direct context model, a bit-history model, and a match model, with weights selected by the neighboring digits and the previous residue pass. For Opus, each symbol is coded by an adaptive context model initialized with the codec's probability tables as priors, and the pyramid vector quantizer (PVQ) indices of the CELT layer are split recursively into pulse counts. At the default level, Balrogg reduces Vorbis music by 16.2\%, Vorbis speech by 10.6%, and Opus speech by 5.4%; xz, zstd, ZPAQ, and bzip3 save at most 4.1% on the same files. Over 48 encoder configurations, files shrink to 66.5--96.1% of their size. Encoding and decoding are symmetric, run at 1.8--3.2~MB/s per core, and use less than 12~MiB of memory.
item.dc:creator: Kamila Szewczyk

item.title: FugaStream: Pipelined Live Volumetric Streaming towards Full Exploitation of Multi-views
item.description: arXiv:2611.32732v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: Live volumetric streaming has become the cornerstone of next-generation immersive applications, enabling users to experience six degrees of freedom (6-DoF). To support interactivity, live volumetric streaming must reconstruct multi-view RGB-D frames into a unified 3D representation while meeting a stringent latency budget, where existing systems are forced to trade reconstruction quality for latency. In this paper, we present FugaStream, the first pipelined live volumetric streaming system that mitigates this trade-off by committing a base representation early and then incrementally merging novel late views. Enabling such functionalities introduces two fundamental challenges: (i) the uncertainty in frame availability, and (ii) the late view updates in a lightweight manner. We address these challenges through two key algorithms: (i) adaptive base commitment control, which determines the base commitment time with the expected reconstruction gain of each missing view against the growing cost of latency, and (ii) base-referenced late view completion, which transmits only the novel regions of late views compared to early committed base, enabling lightweight fusion at the client. We validate the effectiveness of FugaStream on a widely used volumetric dataset and a real-world testbed, demonstrating that FugaStream improves SSIM by 10.9% and IoU by 13.7% over baselines under the same 150 ms budget.
item.dc:creator: Edward Jusuk Kim, Huijeong Choe, Minjae Lee, Chanjeong Park, Kyunghan Lee

item.title: DiaCap: Jointly Learning Who Speaks When for Audiovisual Dialogue Captioning
item.description: arXiv:2611.33153v1 Announce Type: cross Abstract: We present DiaCap, an audiovisual LLM for comprehensive dialogue captioning, which produces the transcript, timestamps, and a visual description of the speaker for every utterance in a video. Considering that utterance timing and audiovisual diarization are tightly coupled, DiaCap unifies the tasks in a single model, trained in two complementary stages. First, we train DiaCap on 225K curated clips, using synthetic captions that densely label every utterance in detail. Second, we further refine the model via reinforcement learning on 2.9K human-corrected clips, using fine-grained feedback that directly evaluates utterance timing, speaker grouping, and speaker binding. On DiaDemBench, which we extend with utterance-level timestamps and subtitle redaction, both DiaCap with off-the-shelf transcripts and its end-to-end variant DiaCap-E2E achieve strong results. Specifically, DiaCap performs on par with Gemini 4 Argon in audiovisual diarization while clearly outperforming it in timestamp accuracy (76.59 vs. 42.76 TIME). It also maintains strong diarization on multilingual and minute-long videos, and transfers to audiovisual question answering.
item.dc:creator: Binfei Ji, Zhiwen Cao, Anqi Yang, Prem Seetharaman, Shuo Yang, Ratheesh Kalarot, Yingyan Celine Lin, Mingze Xu

item.title: ViTrail: Transmission-Inference Co-Design for Vision Transformer-Based Mobile Video Analytics
item.description: arXiv:2601.21362v2 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: Edge-assisted mobile video analytics (MVA) relies on a tight device-edge feedback loop in which captured frames are transmitted for remote inference and the returned results are rendered on the mobile device. Many existing systems optimize frame transmission while treating server-side inference as a fixed cost. This separation becomes inefficient for vision transformer (ViT)-based dense prediction, where high-resolution inputs simultaneously increase network traffic and server computation. We present ViTrail, which co-designs transmission and ViT inference through a shared mixed-resolution representation. The device preserves task-relevant regions at full resolution and downsamples less informative regions before encoding. The server tokenizes each region at its transmitted resolution, so the same regional resolution assignment reduces both the upload payload and the number of tokens processed by the ViT. For dense prediction, ViTrail aligns regions with ViT patches and attention windows and restores a regular feature grid at a configurable stage. At runtime, it selects regional downsampling, compression quality, and the restoration point to maximize predicted installation accuracy, the accuracy of the rendered result when a new remote result is first used for rendering. We build a fully functional prototype on commodity mobile and edge devices and evaluate it in real time across 300 video-trace pairs with real-world 4G/5G traces. ViTrail achieves the highest mean rendering accuracy among the evaluated systems and leads each baseline on 81% to 95% of pairs, while reducing median end-to-end offloading latency by 38% against the most accurate baseline.
item.dc:creator: Miao Zhang, Guanzhen Wu, Hao Fang, Yifei Zhu, Fangxin Wang, Ruixiao Zhang, Linfeng Shen, Jiangchuan Liu

item.title: Pothen: Can Vision-Language Models Tell Where a Cultural Object Comes From?
item.description: arXiv:2604.07338v4 Announce Type: replace-cross Abstract: A cultural object is a trace of the people who made it, and knowing who made it, where, and when shapes how it is catalogued, valued, and returned. Vision-language models now describe such objects for museum collections, yet whether they can recover this knowledge from an image has not been tested. We introduce Pothen, a benchmark of 750 objects from the Metropolitan Museum of Art and the Getty in which a model predicts an object's title, culture, period, origin, and creator from its image alone, scored against curator-written catalogue records by an LLM judge calibrated on human annotation. Across nine models, mean field scores are 36.16% to 49.82%, but all five fields match for only 2.13% to 7.87% of objects. Images raise culture, period, and origin scores by 12.6 to 32.2 points for two models tested without them, and 83.52% of creator matches occur alongside an incorrect field. Models read visual evidence and hold facts about objects but do not bind them into one attribution, and in our error analysis their attributions follow the style an object resembles rather than the record of its making.
item.dc:creator: Yuechen Jiang, Enze Zhang, Mohsinul Kabir, Chenying Lin, Ying Peng, Fengyuan Liu, Qianqian Xie, Stavroula Golfomitsou, Konstantinos Arvanitis, Sophia Ananiadou
